html:
The Manahoac were a Siouan speaking people of the Virginia Piedmont, living along the upper Rappahannock River west of the falls at present Fredericksburg. They numbered perhaps a thousand around 1600.

They were allies of the Monacan and enemies of the Algonquian Powhatan chiefdom of the coast. In 1608 John Smith fought a party of Manahoac while exploring the Rappahannock and learned of them from a captive. Warfare with the Iroquois and disease broke them up in the late 1600s, and survivors joined related peoples such as the Tutelo and Saponi. See also Rappahannock.
